documents.text:
**Thomas Rich**

Thomas Rich (1733-1803) was a British politician and naval officer who served as a Member of Parliament (MP) and held the senior rank of Admiral in the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom. **Early Life and Career**

Thomas Rich was born in 1733 to a prominent family in England. Little is known about his early life, but he began his naval career at a young age, rising through the ranks of the Royal Navy. **Naval Career**

Rich's naval career spanned several decades, during which he served with distinction and earned promotions to increasingly senior ranks. According to the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, Rich was promoted to Rear-Admiral of the Blue in 1794, and later to Vice-Admiral of the Red in 1799. [1] This progression of ranks demonstrates his growing expertise and leadership abilities within the Royal Navy. **Admiral Rank**

The most significant evidence of Rich's admiral rank comes from his appointment as Admiral of the Blue in 1801. [2] This senior rank is one of the highest in the Royal Navy, and Rich's achievement of it is a testament to his dedication and service to the British naval forces. **Parliamentary Career**

In addition to his naval career, Rich also served as a Member of Parliament (MP) for the constituency of Sandwich from 1784 to 1790. [3] This dual role demonstrates his commitment to public service and his ability to balance the demands of both military and political careers. **References**

[1] Oxford Dictionary of National Biography, "Rich, Thomas (1733-1803)" (Oxford University Press, 2004)

[2] The London Gazette, "No. 15415" (February 14, 1801)

[3] History of Parliament Online, "RICH, Thomas (1733-1803)" (Institute of Historical Research, 2019)
